text: INSTITUTION: Bharat College of Engineering DOCUMENT: Academic Regulations, Attendance, and Lab Safety Guidelines (Academic Year 2026-2027) SECTION 1: ATTENDANCE NORMS 1.1 Minimum Attendance Requirement: Every undergraduate student registered for Bachelor of Engineering programs must maintain a minimum overall attendance of 75% across all scheduled theory lectures and practical laboratory sessions. 1.2 Condonation Policy: If a student's attendance falls between 60% and 74.9%, condonation may be considered by the Academic Dean only on genuine medical grounds or sanctioned institutional representation (sports, technical symposiums, university competitions). A certified medical certificate or official permission slip must be submitted to the Department Academic Coordinator within 7 working days of resuming classes. Attendance below 60% cannot be condoned under any circumstances, and the student will be detained from the end-semester examinations for that term. SECTION 2: LABORATORY CONDUCT & SAFETY 2.1 AI and High-Performance Computing (HPC) Lab Rules: - The HPC lab contains dedicated GPU clusters for artificial intelligence, computer vision, and NLP research. - Lab working hours are strictly from 8:30 AM to 5:30 PM, Monday through Friday. - Personal USB flash drives or external bootable media are strictly prohibited on the GPU server nodes to avoid malware injection. - Unattended batch training jobs exceeding 4 continuous hours require prior written authorization from the Lab In-Charge (Prof. K. Sharma, Room 402). - Food, beverages, and open water bottles are strictly prohibited inside the lab enclosure.

DOCUMENT TITLE: Modern NLP Architectures and Semantic Representation MODULE: Natural Language Processing (Semester VII) 1. The Transformer Paradigm The Transformer architecture was introduced in the seminal 2017 paper "Attention Is All You Need" by Ashish Vaswani and colleagues at Google Brain and Google Research. Prior to Transformers, state-of-the-art NLP relied primarily on Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. The fundamental computational bottleneck of recurrent architectures was their strictly sequential processing, which prevented parallelization across time steps and suffered from gradient vanishing over long-distance dependencies. Transformers eliminated recurrence completely, relying entirely on Multi-Head Self-Attention mechanisms. In a multi-head attention module, input embeddings are projected into three separate vector spaces: Queries (Q), Keys (K), and Values (V). Scaled dot-product attention computes attention weights as: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax((Q * K^T) / sqrt(d_k)) * V where d_k is the dimensionality of the key vectors. The scaling factor sqrt(d_k) prevents the dot products from growing excessively large for high dimensions, which would otherwise push the softmax function into regions with tiny gradients. 2. Encoders vs. Decoders Transformer models generally follow one of three architectural variants: - Encoder-Only (e.g., BERT, RoBERTa): Designed for contextual language representation, classification, and token extraction. BERT uses masked language modeling (MLM) and next sentence prediction (NSP) during pre-training to build bidirectional context representations. - Decoder-Only (e.g., GPT-3, LLaMA, Mistral): Designed for autoregressive text generation. These models utilize causal masking in their self-attention layers so that tokens can only attend to previous positions in the sequence. - Encoder-Decoder (e.g., T5, BART): Well-suited for sequence-to-sequence translation, summarization, and text restructuring tasks. 3. Dense Vector Embeddings and Sentence Transformers Standard word embeddings like Word2Vec and GloVe assign static vectors to individual tokens, losing context and polysemy. Sentence Transformers (such as all-MiniLM-L6-v2) produce fixed-size dense representations of entire sentences or passages. The all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model uses a 6-layer architecture with 384 hidden dimensions. It is trained using contrastive learning and distillation to place semantically similar sentences close together in vector space under cosine distance.

PROJECT SPECIFICATION TITLE: Project ShadowSense TEAM LEAD: Vikram Malhotra BUDGET ALLOCATION: 45,000 INR HARDWARE PLATFORM: Raspberry Pi 5 with Coral Edge TPU DEPLOYMENT DEADLINE: November 15, 2026 Project ShadowSense is designed for edge-based acoustic anomaly detection in industrial machinery. It utilizes a custom lightweight 1D-CNN running on an embedded tensor accelerator. Audio sampling is performed at 44.1 kHz using an array of MEMS microphones. The system transmits telemetry over MQTT via local Wi-Fi.
